proposals.relationship: Davidoff credits Douglas’s account of pollution and boundaries with changing her interpretation of domestic service, household routines and respectable status.
proposals.evidence_note: Davidoff’s own 1995 account recalls discovering Purity and Danger in the early 1970s. She connects its concepts to evangelical cleanliness, household space and the incorporation of new wealth, while explaining that subsequent feminist analysis went beyond Douglas. The 1966 book itself was not newly read; 1995 is the acknowledgment, not the date of first influence.
primary_locators: Complete substantive signed essay, paragraphs 1–11, especially paragraphs 5–11; page header distinguishes original 19 May 1995 from update 22 May 2015.

proposals.relationship: As Catherine Hall explains, Davidoff developed Weber’s questions about modernity, power, market position and status through a feminist account of gender and family.
proposals.evidence_note: Hall’s 2015 tribute says Weber probably did more than any other social theorist to frame Davidoff’s thinking. The qualified attribution and Davidoff’s feminist transformation are retained. This is Hall’s substantive interpretation, not a claim that Davidoff accepted an entire Weberian system; the complete tribute and Davidoff’s underlying books remain unread here.
primary_locators: Public publisher Extract, final paragraph beginning Lee’s work is in fact central; overall article pp. 319–328. No exact printed page is inferred from the unpaginated extract.

proposals.relationship: A comparison of their contributions to Family Fortunes highlights Davidoff’s sociological approach and Hall’s Marxist-feminist interests in their joint account of family, gender and class.
proposals.evidence_note: An editorial teaching comparison grounded in Cornelie Usborne’s 2015 account of their complementary approaches, not a direction of influence inferred from coauthorship. Usborne also describes the 1973 project proposal; Hall’s own tribute confirms their coauthorship and describes Davidoff’s methods. Equal authorship is retained. The complete 1987 book and later introductions were not freshly read; the later reissue is not a new original contribution.
primary_locators: Usborne, printed pp. 143–144, especially p. 144 paragraph beginning Leonore Davidoff und Catherine Hall hatten sich 1973; Hall, public Extract, paragraph beginning As a close friend and co-author.

proposals.relationship: McClintock credits Davidoff’s pioneering work but criticizes her Cullwick interpretation for reproducing Munby’s image of control and obscuring the servant’s constrained agency.
proposals.evidence_note: The 1995 argument was read in Plinio Dentzien’s authorized Portuguese translation (2003), printed pp. 13 and 17–20. McClintock acknowledges her debt to Davidoff and to Davidoff and Hall’s joint Family Fortunes, then makes the particular agency criticism of Davidoff’s Munby–Cullwick essay. She also rejects a picture of equal power: agency within severe social inequality is the point. The English chapter and Davidoff’s original essay were not freshly read; this is not a blanket rejection of their work.
primary_locators: Portuguese translation p. 13 n. 3 acknowledges Davidoff and Hall; pp. 17–20 section Sem pigmalião / Agente ambíguo, especially p. 18 and nn. 9–11. Original chapter: Imperial Leather (1995), ch. 3, pp. 132–180; translation: Cadernos Pagu 20 (2003), pp. 7–85.

proposals.relationship: McClintock explicitly draws on Davidoff’s domestic-service research and Davidoff and Hall’s joint Family Fortunes in her account of gender, class and domestic power (1995).
proposals.evidence_note: McClintock’s substantive discussion and explicit acknowledgment in note 3 identify these resources; her later criticism of Davidoff’s particular Cullwick interpretation coexists with this debt. Hall retains equal credit for the joint book. Selected passages were freshly read in Plinio Dentzien’s authorized 2003 Portuguese translation of the 1995 chapter; the English original and the cited Davidoff texts were not freshly read. This does not imply wholesale agreement or personal mentoring.
primary_locators: Portuguese translation printed p. 13 n. 3, with surrounding discussion of Cullwick/Munby; the separate critique is pp. 17–20.
